note.question: Why would a marketplace relinquish its fulfillment margin to let third-party sellers offer pickup or local delivery, and who gains when local fulfillment reveals consumers' geographic differentiation?
note.overview: An online marketplace first selects traditional platform fulfillment or local fulfillment by third-party sellers, after which two sellers set prices simultaneously and heterogeneous consumers choose a seller and fulfillment method.

Lemmas and propositions provide closed-form symmetric equilibrium outcomes by preference-versus-location regime.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In stage 1, the platform chooses traditional online selling or local selling. In stage 2, sellers simultaneously set retail prices. In stage 3, consumers choose a seller and, under local selling, pickup or seller delivery. Traditional platform fulfillment masks location because every consumer experiences the same waiting cost.
